verses.text: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

xrefs.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
[“]I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.

Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

verses.text: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!

xrefs.text: I had planted you like a choice vine from the very best seed. How could you turn yourself before Me into a rotten, wild vine?
But their vine is from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poisonous; their clusters are bitter.
Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.

Still another angel, with authority over the fire, came from the altar and called out in a loud voice to the angel with the sharp sickle, “Swing your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.
Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?

verses.text: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.

xrefs.text: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
Hear the word of the LORD, O house of Jacob, and all you families of the house of Israel.
What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment, you enduring foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel:

verses.text: What more could have been done for My vineyard than I have done for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?

xrefs.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
‘My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!
You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
This is what the LORD says: “What fault did your fathers find in Me that they strayed so far from Me? They followed worthless idols, and became worthless themselves.
Because of the indecency of your uncleanness I tried to cleanse you, but you would not be purified from your filthiness. You will not be pure again until My wrath against you has subsided.

verses.text: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.

xrefs.text: The Lord has rejected all the mighty men in my midst; He has summoned an army against me to crush my young warriors. Like grapes in a winepress, the Lord has trampled the Virgin Daughter of Judah.
Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
“Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”
The LORD will bring a nation from afar, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down upon you like an eagle— a nation whose language you will not understand,

verses.text: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”

xrefs.text: And on that day, in every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver, only briers and thorns will be found.
And this whole land will become a desolate wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth and leaves it in ruins. He will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants—

These witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy, and power to turn the waters into blood and to strike the earth with every kind of plague as often as they wish.
“I also withheld the rain from you when the harvest was three months away. I sent rain on one city but withheld it from another. One field received rain; another without rain withered.

verses.text: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.

xrefs.text: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance.
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!

verses.text: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.

xrefs.text: They covet fields and seize them; they take away houses. They deprive a man of his home, a fellow man of his inheritance.
Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain, to place his nest on high and escape the hand of disaster!
“Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness, and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his countrymen serve without pay, and fails to pay their wages,
Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
And when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

verses.text: I heard the LORD of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.

xrefs.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.
The LORD of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: “Until your dying day, this sin of yours will never be atoned for,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.
The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.

verses.text: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.

xrefs.text: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole out your bread by weight, so that you will eat but not be satisfied.

You have planted much but harvested little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill. You put on clothes but never get warm. You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.”
from that time, when one came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain, there were but ten. When one came to the winepress to draw out fifty baths, there were but twenty.

You expected much, but behold, it amounted to little. And what you brought home, I blew away. Why? declares the LORD of Hosts. Because My house still lies in ruins, while each of you is busy with his own house.
The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.

verses.text: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.

xrefs.text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,
Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.

verses.text: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.

xrefs.text: Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them.
You lie on beds inlaid with ivory, and lounge upon your couches. You dine on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.

Instead, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels from His house were brought to you, and as you drank wine from them with your nobles, wives, and concubines, you praised your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you have failed to glorify the God who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways.

verses.text: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.

xrefs.text: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.

When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.
And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.

verses.text: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!

xrefs.text: But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life— and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.

and wealth indeed betrays him. He is an arrogant man never at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like Death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself and collects all the peoples as his own.
Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

verses.text: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.

xrefs.text: So mankind is brought low, and man is humbled— do not forgive them!
The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
Then I said, “They are only the poor; they have played the fool, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.
Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.

verses.text: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.

xrefs.text: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”

Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.
and on that day you will say: “Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name! Make His works known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.

I will show the holiness of My great name, which has been profaned among the nations— the name you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when I show My holiness in you before their eyes.

verses.text: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.

xrefs.text: So the seacoast will become a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.
For fear of the briers and thorns, you will no longer traverse the hills once tilled by the hoe; they will become places for oxen to graze and sheep to trample.

Herds will lie down in her midst, creatures of every kind. Both the desert owl and screech owl will roost atop her pillars. Their calls will sound from the window, but desolation will lie on the threshold, for He will expose the beams of cedar.
Its abundant harvest goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins. And they rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please. We are in great distress.
Their hearts are callous and insensitive, but I delight in Your law.

verses.text: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,

xrefs.text: And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: They commit adultery and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness. They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.”
For his eyes are too full of conceit to detect or hate his own sin.
For the land is full of adulterers— because of the curse, the land mourns and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up— their course is evil and their power is misused.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority. My people love it so, but what will you do in the end?
Because you have disheartened the righteous with your lies, even though I have caused them no grief, and because you have encouraged the wicked not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives,

verses.text: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”

xrefs.text: “Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel: ‘The days go by, and every vision fails’?
Behold, they keep saying to me, “Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!”

You who tremble at His word, hear the word of the LORD: “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!’ But they will be put to shame.”
They have lied about the LORD and said: “He will not do anything; harm will not come to us; we will not see sword or famine.
Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD! What will the Day of the LORD be for you? It will be darkness and not light.

verses.text: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.

xrefs.text: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.
So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

You have wearied the LORD with your words; yet you ask, “How have we wearied Him?” By saying, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights,” or, “Where is the God of justice?”
They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.

verses.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.

xrefs.text: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited.
Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.

verses.text: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,

xrefs.text: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
Woe to him who gives drink to his neighbors, pouring it from the wineskin until they are drunk, in order to gaze at their nakedness!

These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.
“Come, let me get the wine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorrow will be like today, only far better!”
Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course.

verses.text: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.

xrefs.text: to deprive the poor of fair treatment and withhold justice from the oppressed of My people, to make widows their prey and orphans their plunder.
They band together against the righteous and condemn the innocent to death.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.
Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.

verses.text: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

xrefs.text: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: “Because you have rejected this message, trusting in oppression and relying on deceit,
His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.
Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up. They cannot deliver themselves from the power of the flame. There will be no coals to warm them or fire to sit beside.

verses.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lie like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

xrefs.text: Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
And Jezebel’s body will lie like dung in the field on the plot of ground at Jezreel, so that no one can say: This is Jezebel.’

Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men; He has no compassion on their fatherless and widows. For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.

verses.text: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold— how speedily and swiftly they come!

xrefs.text: I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them; and they will be as numerous as they once were.
On that day the LORD will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.
The LORD will bring a nation from afar, from the ends of the earth, to swoop down upon you like an eagle— a nation whose language you will not understand,
All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.
He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

verses.text: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.

xrefs.text: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.
He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:
Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand.

verses.text: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.

xrefs.text: Your arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s foes; the nations fall beneath your feet.

The shields of his mighty men are red; the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet. The fittings of the chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the spears of cypress have been brandished.
“Son of man, prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord says: ‘A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished—
If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword; He has bent and strung His bow.
Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.

verses.text: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away, and no one can rescue it.

xrefs.text: But this is a people plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Send them back!”
Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?
Listen to the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is in ruins. Listen to the roaring of the young lions, for the thickets of the Jordan are destroyed.

Then the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it passes through, with no one to rescue them.
He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness— who dares to rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you.”

verses.text: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.

xrefs.text: Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into utter darkness.
Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.
I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light.
And the fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness, and men began to gnaw their tongues in anguish
And I watched as the Lamb opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black like sackcloth of goat hair, and the whole moon turned blood red,
